paragraphs: The 118i has been part of the 1 Series range since 2011, spanning two generations under one badge. The earlier F20/F21 generation (2011 to 2019) uses the N13 — a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine, developed in partnership with PSA and shared across a number of BMW models of that era. From 2019, the F40-generation 118i switched to the B38 — a 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol unit that's part of BMW's newer modular engine family. The B38 is a different design entirely, not an evolution of the N13. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 118i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the 118i from 2011 to 2019 (F20/F21 generation). No widely-reported engine issue for this variant — we still recommend a full inspection before any long journey. We replace timing chain components, bearings and gaskets as standard on every N13 rebuild.

The current-generation 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol engine, fitted from 2019 to 2024. This is BMW's newer modular engine design, generally considered more reliable than the N13 generation. We service it to the same standard as our other 118i rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the 118i spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N13 part will work on a B38 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N13 or B38) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 118i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
